# Comparison of Existing Systems

**Purpose:** Compare MRBS, Skedda, and LibCal against the key requirements of AITU Booking.

## 1. Comparison Table

| Criterion | MRBS (Meeting Room Booking System) | Skedda | LibCal |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Room Search** | Browse rooms by area. | Search, filters, and floor plans. | Room booking; search depends on configuration. |
| **Schedule and Availability** | Booking calendar. | Calendar views and current availability. | Room and consultation calendars. |
| **Booking Management** | Create and edit own bookings. | Create, edit, and cancel bookings. | Book rooms and schedule appointments. |
| **Staff Consultations** | Dedicated workflow not confirmed. | Dedicated workflow not confirmed. | Supports one-to-one consultations. |
| **Roles and Permissions** | User and administrator permissions. | Configurable rules and access. | Configurable permissions. |
| **Mobile Access** | Web interface; dedicated app not confirmed. | Mobile website and app. | Mobile-friendly web interface. |
| **Administration** | Manage rooms and bookings. | Manage spaces, rules, and reports. | Manage bookings, staff availability, and equipment. |
| **Notifications** | Specific notification workflows require verification. | Reminder settings require verification. | Email notifications and reminders. |
| **AITU-Specific Processes** | PDF schedule import and key/ID-card workflow not confirmed. | Compatibility with AITU processes not confirmed. | Compatibility with AITU schedules and key handling not confirmed. |

## 2. Key Findings

The comparison shows that existing systems support room booking and availability management, but the reviewed solutions do not confirm an integrated workflow for classroom reservations and staff consultation scheduling. Support for AITU-specific requirements, such as importing schedules in the "10+2 weeks" format and managing classroom keys using ID cards, has also not been confirmed.

## 3. Conclusion

The comparison of existing systems reveals a gap between standard room booking functionality and the specific needs of AITU. Although the reviewed solutions cover individual booking-related tasks, the available evidence does not confirm that any of them supports all the required processes in one system. Therefore, none of the reviewed analogues can be confirmed as a complete solution for the identified AITU scenario.
